version.changelog: 出版级中文长篇小说全流程创作技能包，网络连载与实体出版双标准

llm.summary: This is a disclosed Chinese novel-writing assistant that creates local project files and trackers, with no evidence of hidden data access or exfiltration.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md, README files, references, and helper scripts consistently support long-form Chinese fiction planning, drafting, foreshadowing tracking, and quality checks.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad for creative-writing requests and defaults to a publication-grade Chinese workflow, so users may want to confirm lightweight story requests do not enter the full project workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package uses normal skill installation instructions and contains markdown references, SVG banners, and Python helper scripts; no custom installer, install-time execution, obfuscation, or package-install behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local reads of bundled references and writes under ~/.qclaw/workspace/novels/<book-name>/ are proportionate for persistent novel project management, but the scripts do not validate path-like book names.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill stores outlines, chapters, state.json, and tracker JSON locally for continuity; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned, with no credential access, background worker, privilege escalation, network calls, or destructive deletion behavior found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this if you want a structured, persistent novel-writing workflow. Expect local files to be created and updated under ~/.qclaw/workspace/novels/ for outlines, chapters, foreshadowing, conflicts, and progress state. Use simple book names without slashes or path components, and ask the agent to confirm before creating or modifying project files if you only want a quick story draft.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill’s local file reads and writes are core to the novel-project workflow and are disclosed in SKILL.md and README; lack of explicit permission metadata and path validation is guidance-level risk, not Review-level evidence by itself.
[TP4] unexpected: The claimed purpose mismatch is not supported: the scripts are helpers, while the skill instructions and bundled references supply the planning, writing, and quality-control workflow.
[SQP-2] expected: Project scaffolding and persistent state are expected for this workflow and the target directory structure is documented, though explicit confirmation before file creation would improve user control.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger scope is broad but remains within creative writing; users should avoid invoking the full project workflow for one-off drafts unless desired.
[SQP-3] expected: The default Chinese publication-style mode matches the stated skill purpose, but users should specify language and style if they want a different writing mode.
[RA2] expected: Persistent state and foreshadowing tracking are intentional features for long-form writing continuity; no background persistence, autonomous worker, or hidden retention mechanism was found.
